Marionette

Deterministic I/O and simulation testing for Zig.

Long term, Marionette is aiming to be the deterministic std.Io for Zig: production libraries accept std.Io, and tests swap in Marionette's deterministic implementation. Today, Marionette ships the simulator, trace, fault, disk, and network primitives that make that direction concrete.

Marionette already runs real, unmodified Zig code under deterministic simulation: a storage engine (xit-vcs/xitdb) and a cooperative-concurrency library (g41797/mailbox), both with seed-reproducible replay, and has surfaced reproducible recovery and correctness counterexamples in the process.

Today the demonstrated tiers are:

  • deterministic std.Io.File storage simulation with crash/torn-write faults;
  • cooperative std.Io task scheduling for Mutex / Condition code;
  • scheduler-backed std.Io.net streams with deterministic latency, partitions, timeouts, healing, and retry;
  • scheduler-aware disk operations that park tasks behind earlier deadlines;
  • experimental typed message modeling with deterministic loss, latency, and partitions.

Write production-shaped code against std.Io wherever possible, and add small Marionette handles only when the application actually needs them. In tests, drive control to inject faults. Production.env() supplies host I/O and the rooted real disk; application-owned protocol seams receive Marionette endpoints only in simulation.

const mar = @import("marionette");

fn writeAndRecover(io: std.Io, root: std.Io.Dir) !KVStore {
    var store = try KVStore.init(io, root);
    try store.put(1, 41, .sync);
    try store.put(2, 99, .no_sync);
    try store.recover(.strict);
    return store;
}

// In simulation: deterministic, fault-injectable, replayable from a seed.
var world = try mar.World.init(std.testing.allocator, .{ .seed = 0xC0FFEE });
defer world.deinit();

const sim = try world.simulate(.{ .disk = .{ .sector_size = 16 } });
var sim_store = try writeAndRecover(sim.env.io(), std.Io.Dir.cwd());

// In production: real disk, same code path.
var tmp = std.testing.tmpDir(.{});
defer tmp.cleanup();

var production = try mar.Production.init(.{
    .allocator = std.testing.allocator,
    .root_dir = tmp.dir,
    .io = std.testing.io,
});
defer production.deinit();

const prod_env = production.env();
var prod_store = try writeAndRecover(prod_env.io(), tmp.dir);

For file-backed code like this, that parity is the point. You don't write a "simulator version" of your code. You write your code behind Marionette-owned authorities, and Marionette gives you a deterministic environment to run it in.

Why

Distributed and storage systems fail in ways that are hard to reproduce: a torn write under crash, a network partition during quorum, a race between two timers. By the time you have a stack trace, the conditions that caused the bug are gone.

Deterministic simulation testing turns those bugs into seeds. Every run is reproducible. Every failure is replayable. You compress weeks of fuzz-testing into seconds, and when something breaks in CI, the seed alone is enough to debug it.

Marionette brings that approach to Zig. It's inspired by the techniques behind FoundationDB, TigerBeetle, and Antithesis, but designed to be a drop-in library, not a framework you build your system around.

A complete example

Here's a WAL recovery test that crashes the disk mid-write, corrupts a sector, and asserts that committed records survive while unsynced ones don't.

const Case = mar.SimCase(WalStore);

pub fn scenario(case: *Case) !void {
    const store = &case.app;
    const disk = case.control().disk;

    try store.put(committed_key, committed_value, .sync);
    try disk.setFaults(.{ .crash_lost_write_rate = .always() });
    try store.put(volatile_key, volatile_value, .no_sync);
    try disk.crash();
    try disk.restart();
    try disk.corruptSector(wal_path, record_size);
    try store.reopen();
    try store.recover(.strict);
}

pub const checks = [_]mar.StateCheck(Case){
    .{ .name = "synced records recover, unsynced records are rejected", .check = recoveredStateIsSafe },
};

test "wal recovery" {
    try mar.expectSimPass(.{
        .allocator = std.testing.allocator,
        .seed = 0xC0FFEE,
        .simulate = .{},
        .init = WalStore.init,
        .scenario = scenario,
        .checks = &checks,
    });
}

test "wal recovery fuzz" {
    try mar.expectSimFuzz(.{
        .allocator = std.testing.allocator,
        .seed = 0xC0FFEE,
        .seeds = 16,
        .simulate = .{},
        .init = WalStore.init,
        .scenario = scenario,
        .checks = &checks,
    });
}

mar.SimCase(App) is the standard wrapper for simulation tests: init receives mar.Sim, scenario receives *mar.SimCase(App), and app state lives at case.app. Harnesses that need lower-level World access or unusual ownership drive mar.World directly.

Three pieces, either way:

  • init sets up app state from mar.Sim.
  • scenario drives the action through case.app and simulator authorities such as case.control().
  • checks assert invariants on the final state, usually through *const mar.SimCase(App).

expectSimPass runs twice with one fixed seed and compares the traces. expectSimFuzz requires a nonzero seeds count and performs the same replay check for each derived seed. expectSimFailure asserts that a deliberately buggy scenario reaches a replayable failure, useful for proving your checker actually works. Custom harnesses that outgrow these helpers drive mar.World directly.

The two surfaces: io and control

Every Marionette test has two halves.

io is what production-shaped storage code should usually see. In simulation, sim.env.io() returns Marionette's deterministic std.Io backend. In production, production.env().io() returns the host std.Io supplied at setup. Application code that wants trace events should accept a narrow mar.Recorder, not all of mar.Env.

var store = try KVStore.init(io, root, recorder);
try store.put(1, 41, .sync);

control is what your test code uses to inject faults. It's only available in simulation. It mirrors env's structure: every resource has a control surface.

try control.disk.crash();
try control.disk.corruptSector(path, offset);
try control.network.partition(&side_a, &side_b);
try control.network.setLossiness(.{ .drop_rate = .percent(20) });
try control.network.heal();

Env is still the harness-owned bundle that supplies io(), recorder(), clock/random helpers, and remaining Marionette capabilities. Code that only needs file I/O should prefer std.Io so it stays ordinary Zig code.

Distributed simulation

Network simulation works the same way. Here's a partition test against a toy replicated register:

fn partitionScenario(case: *Case) !void {
    const isolated = [_]mar.NodeId{0};
    const majority = [_]mar.NodeId{ 1, 2, client_node_id };

    try case.control().network.partition(&isolated, &majority);
    try case.app.write(.{ .version = 1, .value = 41, .retry_limit = 2 });

    try case.control().network.heal();
    try case.app.write(.{ .version = 1, .value = 41, .retry_limit = 1 });

    try checkReplicaCommitted(&case.app, 0, 1, 41);
}

Messages have configurable loss, latency, clogs, and partition dynamics through focused control.network calls such as setLossiness(...), setLatency(...), and setPartitionDynamics(...). Application code sends through a node-scoped endpoint with endpoint.send(to, message) and receives with while (try endpoint.receive()) |envelope|.

std.Io.net client/server validation

The external-style std_io_net_kv example imports only std and implements a fixed-frame PUT/GET service over std.Io.net. In simulation, node-scoped std.Io handles come from sim.envForNode(node).io(), so reconnecting sockets keep the same process identity instead of consuming topology. Its Marionette harness partitions the client from a queued response, surfaces the dropped delivery as error.Timeout, heals the link, and retries the request. A correct server deduplicates the retry; a planted buggy mode applies it twice and violates an exact revision oracle.

Simulation processes are first-class runtime owners. sim.killProcess(node) cancels that node's scheduler-backed Io.async/Io.concurrent work, closes process-local files/listeners/connections, and wakes surviving TCP peers with reset errors. sim.registerProcess(node, lifecycle) plus sim.restartProcess(node) reruns a registered initializer with that node's Env after volatile state has been discarded by the lifecycle's on_kill callback. Explicit process kill leaves the shared disk model intact; disk crash is the operation that first applies pending-write crash faults, then uses the same process-kill path.

zig build validate-std-io-net-kv
zig build run-example -- std-io-net-kv --seed 12648430 --trace
zig build run-example -- std-io-net-kv-bug \
  --seed 12648430 --trace --expect-failure

See Testing std.Io.net Code Deterministically for the trace and exact supported boundary. This is an external-style capability demonstration, not a third-party SUT finding.

Cooperative concurrency

Marionette has scheduler-backed cooperative std.Io tasks and futex waits for Mutex / Condition code. Io.async and Io.concurrent run as deterministic simulator tasks, and awaiting from either a task or the scenario drives the same scheduler. The pinned g41797/mailbox validation target runs unmodified and exercises timed receive, send/wake, same-deadline timeout ordering, and byte-identical same-seed replay. The internal validate-bounded-queue target adds a canonical FIFO oracle and a planted lost-wakeup deadlock to demonstrate concurrency bug detection without counting it as an external SUT finding. This is cooperative std.Io concurrency, not preemptive OS thread or memory-model testing; see Std.Io Direction for the exact boundary.

Ochi storage validation

The optional validate-ochi target composes the pinned, unmodified ochi-team/ochi storage implementation with mar.SimCase. It starts the store, ingests a line, flushes index and data tables, queries the inserted data, exercises atomic catalog replacement, crashes the simulated disk, reopens Ochi, and queries the data again through Marionette's deterministic std.Io. Ochi is a lazy dependency and this target is not part of the default test step. The validation runs one simulation per process because Ochi's private temporary-file counter intentionally persists across in-process runs.

zig build validate-ochi

HTTP library validation

The optional validate-dusty target runs the pinned, unmodified lalinsky/dusty HTTP client/server library through Marionette's deterministic std.Io. dusty's real Server.listen accept loop runs as a simulated task: its router, llhttp parser, and connection pool serve a keep-alive GET/POST pair plus a second connection over simulated std.Io.net streams with injected latency, and the harness then shuts the server down through cooperative cancellation. Two shutdown shapes are validated: a clean shutdown where error.Canceled lands in dusty's accept park and the drain finds no active connections, and a hung-connection shutdown where a keep-alive handler is still parked in a read, dusty's drain times out, and its deferred Group.cancel sweeps the parked handler on the way out. Fault scenarios partition the link before and during a response, pin dusty's observed error.Timeout contract, heal and retry against an exact body oracle, and sweep every chunk cut point while rejecting short-success partial responses. Everything replays byte-identically from the same seed. dusty is a lazy dependency and this target is not part of the default test step.

zig build validate-dusty

This is an external-style capability demonstration of the std.Io.net boundary, not a third-party SUT finding. The 0.6 slice chain is complete: pooled keep-alive reuse and large byte-exact transfers landed with the pool and transfer scenarios, which also found two confirmed dusty bugs (see FOUND_BUGS.md), and opt-in task start jitter lets seed sweeps explore start orderings such as connect-before-listen races.

Queue client validation

The optional validate-beanstalkz target runs the pinned, unmodified g41797/beanstalkz beanstalkd work-queue client against a harness-owned in-memory beanstalkd that speaks the text protocol over simulated std.Io.net streams. It covers a produce/consume round trip with bury/kick state transitions, sequential connection churn (fresh connect, put, quit, shutdown(.both), close cycles drained in FIFO order), a blocking reserve-with-timeout parked across a five-second virtual publish delay, and a server-process crash under a parked reserve: the surviving client wakes with a reset that surfaces as the library's CommunicationFailure contract, then a registered process restart recovers on a fresh incarnation. Everything replays byte-identically from the same seed. beanstalkz is a lazy dependency and this target is not part of the default test step.

zig build validate-beanstalkz

Traces

Every run produces a structured trace. When a check fails, you get the full sequence of events that led to the violation, plus the seed to reproduce it.

register.write.start version=1 value=41 retry_limit=8
register.message kind=propose to=0 version=1 value=41
replica.accept replica=0 version=1 value=41 accepted=true
register.message kind=propose to=1 version=1 value=41
replica.accept replica=1 version=1 value=41 accepted=true
register.write.quorum version=1 value=41 acks=2
register.invariant_violation kind=committed_divergence replica=1 ...

You write trace records with mar.Recorder or, inside harness-shaped code, env.record(...). Application code, scenario code, and checks can all record. Failed runs print the trace automatically. Passing runs hand it back to you so you can persist it, diff it, or feed it to whatever observability you already have.

Status

Marionette is early. This is a 0.x release: there is no API stability guarantee before 1.0. The intended-stable surface today is World, Env, Control, SimCase, runSimCase / expectSim*, Disk, SimDisk, RealDisk, Production, and Recorder. The public Endpoint(Message) message-modeling surface remains experimental while its ownership and transport contract are validated against a real SUT.

The simulator currently models clock, deterministic randomness, disk, a directory-aware std.Io.File/Dir subset, experimental typed message modeling, a narrow scheduler-backed std.Io.net stream subset with accept/read suspension plus latency and send-time loss, delivery-time partitions, deterministic healing, and literal-only host lookup (an unmodified std.http.Client runs against simulated servers; real DNS stays unsupported), and cooperative std.Io tasks, groups, and futex waits for Mutex / Condition code, validated against the pinned g41797/mailbox and g41797/beanstalkz targets and the internal bounded-queue capability demo, plus the pinned Ochi storage target. It does not model arbitrary OS thread scheduling or memory-level concurrency; code that depends on those needs separate testing. The simulator also models deterministic allocation faults through Env.allocator() and cooperative cancellation: Future.cancel and Group.cancel deliver error.Canceled at futex, sleep, and net suspension points following std.Io's one-shot protocol. A one-shot sim.transitionToLiveness(core) ends the fault regime so bounded runs can prove the core makes progress once faults stop. Networking has two sibling testing altitudes. Node-scoped std.Io.net is the canonical literal same-code path for codecs, framing, partial I/O, and stream lifecycle. Experimental Endpoint(Message) explores protocol/state-machine behavior above the wire; production uses an application-owned transport seam, and Marionette does not claim that the real transport runs through the endpoint model. The former Marionette-owned production adapters were removed in 0.6. Queue suspension and broader scheduler parity are planned.

Scheduler-backed fibers are tested on Linux and macOS. The x86_64 Windows fiber path is deliberately disabled until its Win64 entry ABI has execution coverage. RealDisk.syncDir returns error.DirectorySyncUnsupported because Zig 0.16 does not expose a portable directory-sync operation; it never reports durability that it did not perform.

If you're building something where determinism matters and you want to try it, the examples/ directory is the best place to start. Open issues and PRs welcome.

Install

zig fetch --save https://github.com/sb2bg/marionette/archive/refs/tags/v0.6.1.tar.gz

Then wire the module into your test build in build.zig and import it:

const marionette = b.dependency("marionette", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});
tests_module.addImport("marionette", marionette.module("marionette"));
const mar = @import("marionette");

Requires Zig 0.16.x.

Acknowledgments

Marionette stands on the shoulders of FoundationDB's simulation testing, TigerBeetle's VOPR, and the broader DST tradition. The bugs they catch are bugs everyone has; this library tries to make catching them easy in Zig.

The simulator currently models clock, deterministic randomness, disk, a directory-aware std.Io.File/Dir subset, experimental typed message modeling, a narrow scheduler-backed std.Io.net stream subset with accept/read suspension plus latency and send-time loss, delivery-time partitions, deterministic healing, and literal-only host lookup (an unmodified std.http.Client runs against simulated servers; real DNS stays unsupported), and cooperative std.Io tasks, groups, and futex waits for Mutex / Condition code, validated against the pinned g41797/mailbox and g41797/beanstalkz targets and the internal bounded-queue capability demo, plus the pinned Ochi storage target. It does not model arbitrary OS thread scheduling or memory-level concurrency; code that depends on those needs separate testing. The simulator also models deterministic allocation faults through Env.allocator() and cooperative cancellation: Future.cancel and Group.cancel deliver error.Canceled at futex, sleep, and net suspension points following std.Io's one-shot protocol. A one-shot sim.transitionToLiveness(core) ends the fault regime so bounded runs can prove the core makes progress once faults stop. Networking has two sibling testing altitudes. Node-scoped std.Io.net is the canonical literal same-code path for codecs, framing, partial I/O, and stream lifecycle. Experimental Endpoint(Message) explores protocol/state-machine behavior above the wire; production uses an application-owned transport seam, and Marionette does not claim that the real transport runs through the endpoint model. The former Marionette-owned production adapters were removed in 0.6. Queue suspension and broader scheduler parity are planned. Scheduler-backed fibers are tested on Linux and macOS. The x86_64 Windows fiber path is deliberately disabled until its Win64 entry ABI has execution coverage. RealDisk.syncDir returns error.DirectorySyncUnsupported because Zig 0.16 does not expose a portable directory-sync operation; it never reports durability that it did not perform. If you're building something where determinism matters and you want to try it, the examples/ directory is the best place to start. Open issues and PRs welcome. Install zig fetch --save https://github.com/sb2bg/marionette/archive/refs/tags/v0.6.1.tar.gz Then wire the module into your test build in build.zig and import it: const marionette = b.dependency("marionette", .{ .target = target, .optimize = optimize, }); tests_module.addImport("marionette", marionette.module("marionette")); const mar = @import("marionette"); Requires Zig 0.16.x. Acknowledgments Marionette stands on the shoulders of FoundationDB's simulation testing, TigerBeetle's VOPR, and the broader DST tradition. The bugs they catch are bugs everyone has; this library tries to make catching them easy in Zig. License MIT

blocks.html_en: Marionette has scheduler-backed cooperative std.Io tasks and futex waits for Mutex / Condition code. Io.async and Io.concurrent run as deterministic simulator tasks, and awaiting from either a task or the scenario drives the same scheduler. The pinned g41797/mailbox validation target runs unmodified and exercises timed receive, send/wake, same-deadline timeout ordering, and byte-identical same-seed replay. The internal validate-bounded-queue target adds a canonical FIFO oracle and a planted lost-wakeup deadlock to demonstrate concurrency bug detection without counting it as an external SUT finding. blocks.html_en: The optional validate-dusty target runs the pinned, unmodified lalinsky/dusty HTTP client/server library through Marionette's deterministic std.Io. dusty's real Server.listen accept loop runs as a simulated task: its router, llhttp parser, and connection pool serve a keep-alive GET/POST pair plus a second connection over simulated std.Io.net streams with injected latency, and the harness then shuts the server down through cooperative cancellation. Two shutdown shapes are validated: a clean shutdown where error.Canceled lands in dusty's accept park and the drain finds no active connections, and a hung-connection shutdown where a keep-alive handler is still parked in a read, dusty's drain times out, and its deferred Group.cancel sweeps the parked handler on the way out. Fault scenarios partition the link before and during a response, pin dusty's observed error.Timeout contract, heal and retry against an exact body oracle, and sweep every chunk cut point while rejecting short-success partial responses. Everything replays byte-identically from the same seed. dusty is a lazy dependency and this target is not part of the default test step.

content_html_zh:
木偶

Zig 的确定性 I/O 和模拟测试。

从长远来看，Marionette 的目标是成为 Zig 的确定性 std.Io：生产库接受 std.Io，并在 Marionette 的确定性实现中进行测试交换。 如今，Marionette 提供了模拟器、跟踪、故障、磁盘和网络原语，使该方向变得具体。

Marionette 已经在确定性模拟下运行真实的、未经修改的 Zig 代码：存储引擎 (xit-vcs/xitdb) 和协作并发库 (g41797/mailbox)，两者都具有种子可重现的重放，并且在此过程中出现了可重现的恢复和正确性反例。

今天展示的层级是：

  • 具有崩溃/撕裂写入故障的确定性 std.Io.File 存储模拟；
  • 互斥/条件代码的协作 std.Io 任务调度；
  • 调度程序支持的 std.Io.net 流具有确定性延迟、分区、超时、修复和重试；
  • 调度程序感知的磁盘操作将任务停放在较早的截止日期之后；
  • 具有确定性丢失、延迟和分区的实验类型消息建模。

尽可能针对 std.Io 编写生产型代码，并仅在应用程序实际需要时添加小型 Marionette 句柄。 在测试中，驱动控制注入故障。 Production.env() 提供主机 I/O 和 root 真实磁盘；应用程序拥有的协议接缝仅在模拟中接收 Marionette 端点。

const mar = @import("marionette");

fn writeAndRecover(io: std.Io, root: std.Io.Dir) !KVStore {
    var store = try KVStore.init(io, root);
    try store.put(1, 41, .sync);
    try store.put(2, 99, .no_sync);
    try store.recover(.strict);
    return store;
}

// In simulation: deterministic, fault-injectable, replayable from a seed.
var world = try mar.World.init(std.testing.allocator, .{ .seed = 0xC0FFEE });
defer world.deinit();

const sim = try world.simulate(.{ .disk = .{ .sector_size = 16 } });
var sim_store = try writeAndRecover(sim.env.io(), std.Io.Dir.cwd());

// In production: real disk, same code path.
var tmp = std.testing.tmpDir(.{});
defer tmp.cleanup();

var production = try mar.Production.init(.{
    .allocator = std.testing.allocator,
    .root_dir = tmp.dir,
    .io = std.testing.io,
});
defer production.deinit();

const prod_env = production.env();
var prod_store = try writeAndRecover(prod_env.io(), tmp.dir);

对于像这样的文件支持的代码，奇偶校验就是关键。 您不会编写代码的“模拟器版本”。 您在 Marionette 拥有的权限后面编写代码，Marionette 为您提供一个确定性的环境来运行它。

Why

分布式和存储系统的故障方式难以重现：崩溃时写入中断、仲裁期间的网络分区、两个计时器之间的竞争。 当您获得堆栈跟踪时，导致错误的条件已经消失。

确定性模拟测试将这些错误转化为种子。 每次运行都是可重复的。 每一次失败都可以重演。 您将数周的模糊测试压缩为几秒钟，当 CI 中出现问题时，仅种子就足以对其进行调试。

Marionette 将这种方法带到了 Zig 身上。 它的灵感来自 FoundationDB、TigerBeetle 和 Antithesis 背后的技术，但被设计为一个嵌入式库，而不是您构建系统的框架。

一个完整的例子

下面是一个 WAL 恢复测试，它会在写入过程中使磁盘崩溃、损坏扇区，并断言已提交的记录会存活，而未同步的记录则不会。

const Case = mar.SimCase(WalStore);

pub fn scenario(case: *Case) !void {
    const store = &case.app;
    const disk = case.control().disk;

    try store.put(committed_key, committed_value, .sync);
    try disk.setFaults(.{ .crash_lost_write_rate = .always() });
    try store.put(volatile_key, volatile_value, .no_sync);
    try disk.crash();
    try disk.restart();
    try disk.corruptSector(wal_path, record_size);
    try store.reopen();
    try store.recover(.strict);
}

pub const checks = [_]mar.StateCheck(Case){
    .{ .name = "synced records recover, unsynced records are rejected", .check = recoveredStateIsSafe },
};

test "wal recovery" {
    try mar.expectSimPass(.{
        .allocator = std.testing.allocator,
        .seed = 0xC0FFEE,
        .simulate = .{},
        .init = WalStore.init,
        .scenario = scenario,
        .checks = &checks,
    });
}

test "wal recovery fuzz" {
    try mar.expectSimFuzz(.{
        .allocator = std.testing.allocator,
        .seed = 0xC0FFEE,
        .seeds = 16,
        .simulate = .{},
        .init = WalStore.init,
        .scenario = scenario,
        .checks = &checks,
    });
}

mar.SimCase(App) 是模拟测试的标准包装器：init 接收 mar.Sim，scenario 接收 *mar.SimCase(App)，并且应用程序状态位于 case.app。 需要较低级别的世界访问权限或不寻常所有权的线束直接驱动 mar.World。

三件，无论哪种方式：

  • init 从 mar.Sim 设置应用程序状态。
  • 场景通过 case.app 和模拟器权限（例如 case.control()）驱动操作。
  • 检查最终状态的断言不变量，通常通过 *const mar.SimCase(App)。

ExpectSimPass 使用一个固定种子运行两次并比较痕迹。 ExpectSimFuzz 需要非零种子计数，并对每个派生种子执行相同的重播检查。 ExpectSimFailure 断言故意出现错误的场景会导致可重播的失败，这对于证明您的检查器确实有效非常有用。 超出这些帮助器的定制线束可以直接驱动 mar.World。

两个表面：io 和 control

每个木偶测试都有两部分。

io 是生产型存储代码通常应该看到的。 在模拟中，sim.env.io() 返回 Marionette 的确定性 std.Io 后端。 在生产环境中， production.env().io() 返回设置时提供的主机 std.Io。 需要跟踪事件的应用程序代码应该接受狭窄的 mar.Recorder，而不是全部 mar.Env。

var store = try KVStore.init(io, root, recorder);
try store.put(1, 41, .sync);

控制是您的测试代码用来注入错误的内容。 它仅在模拟中可用。 它反映了 env 的结构：每个资源都有一个控制面。

try control.disk.crash();
try control.disk.corruptSector(path, offset);
try control.network.partition(&side_a, &side_b);
try control.network.setLossiness(.{ .drop_rate = .percent(20) });
try control.network.heal();

Env 仍然是harness 拥有的包，提供 io()、recorder()、时钟/随机助手和剩余的 Marionette 功能。 仅需要文件 I/O 的代码应该更喜欢 std.Io，因此它仍然是普通的 Zig 代码。

分布式仿真

网络模拟的工作原理相同。 这是针对玩具复制寄存器的分区测试：

fn partitionScenario(case: *Case) !void {
    const isolated = [_]mar.NodeId{0};
    const majority = [_]mar.NodeId{ 1, 2, client_node_id };

    try case.control().network.partition(&isolated, &majority);
    try case.app.write(.{ .version = 1, .value = 41, .retry_limit = 2 });

    try case.control().network.heal();
    try case.app.write(.{ .version = 1, .value = 41, .retry_limit = 1 });

    try checkReplicaCommitted(&case.app, 0, 1, 41);
}

通过集中控制网络调用（例如 setLossiness(...)、setLatency(...) 和 setPartitionDynamics(...)），消息具有可配置的丢失、延迟、阻塞和分区动态。 应用程序代码使用端点.send(to, message) 通过节点范围的端点发送并使用 while 接收（尝试端点.receive()) |envelope|。

std.Io.net 客户端/服务器验证

外部样式 std_io_net_kv 示例仅导入 std 并通过 std.Io.net 实现固定帧 PUT/GET 服务。 在模拟中，节点范围的 std.Io 句柄来自 sim.envForNode(node).io()，因此重新连接套接字会保持相同的进程标识，而不是消耗拓扑。 其 Marionette 工具将客户端与排队响应分开，将丢弃的交付显示为 error.Timeout，修复链接并重试请求。 正确的服务器去重重试；植入的越野车模式应用了两次并且违反了精确的修订预言。

模拟进程是一流的运行时所有者。 sim.killProcess(node) 取消该节点的调度程序支持的 Io.async/Io.concurrent 工作，关闭进程本地文件/侦听器/连接，并通过重置错误唤醒幸存的 TCP 对等点。 在生命周期的 on_kill 回调丢弃易失性状态后，sim.registerProcess(node,lifecycle) 加上 sim.restartProcess(node) 使用该节点的 Env 重新运行已注册的初始化程序。 显式进程终止使共享磁盘模型保持完整；磁盘崩溃是首先应用挂起写入崩溃故障，然后使用相同的进程终止路径的操作。

zig build validate-std-io-net-kv
zig build run-example -- std-io-net-kv --seed 12648430 --trace
zig build run-example -- std-io-net-kv-bug \
  --seed 12648430 --trace --expect-failure

有关跟踪和确切支持的边界，请参阅确定性测试 std.Io.net 代码。 这是外部式的功能演示，而不是第三方 SUT 发现。

合作并发

Marionette 具有调度程序支持的协作 std.Io 任务，并且 futex 等待互斥/条件代码。 Io.async 和 Io.concurrent 作为确定性模拟器任务运行，并等待任务或场景驱动相同的调度程序。 固定的 g41797/邮箱验证目标未经修改地运行，并执行定时接收、发送/唤醒、相同截止日期超时排序和字节相同相同种子重放。 内部 validate-bounded-queue 目标添加了规范的 FIFO 预言机和植入的丢失唤醒死锁，以演示并发错误检测，而不将其视为外部 SUT 发现。 这是协作性 std.Io 并发，而不是抢占式操作系统线程或内存模型测试；有关确切边界，请参阅 Std.Io 方向。

Ochi 存储验证

可选的 validate-ochi 目标与 mar.SimCase 组成固定的、未修改的 ochi-team/ochi 存储实现。 它启动存储、摄取一行、刷新索引和数据表、查询插入的数据、执行原子目录替换、崩溃模拟磁盘、重新打开 Ochi，并通过 Marionette 的确定性 std.Io 再次查询数据。 Ochi 是一个惰性依赖项，此目标不是默认测试步骤的一部分。 验证对每个进程运行一次模拟，因为 Ochi 的私有临时文件计数器有意在进程内运行中保持不变。

zig build validate-ochi

HTTP 库验证

可选的 validate-dusty 目标通过 Marionette 的确定性 std.Io 运行固定的、未修改的 lalinsky/dusty HTTP 客户端/服务器库。 Dusty 的真实 Server.listen 接受循环作为模拟任务运行：它的路由器、llhttp 解析器和连接池提供保持活动的 GET/POST 对以及通过注入延迟的模拟 std.Io.net 流的第二个连接，然后该工具通过协作取消来关闭服务器。 验证了两种关闭形状：干净关闭，其中 error.Canceled 落在 Dusty 的接受公园中，并且 Drain 未发现任何活动连接；以及挂起连接关闭，其中保持活动处理程序仍停放在读取中，Dusty 的 Drain 超时，其延迟的 Group.cancel 在退出时清除停放的处理程序。 故障场景在响应之前和响应期间对链路进行分区，固定dusty观察到的错误。超时合约，针对精确的身体预言进行修复和重试，并扫描每个块切割点，同时拒绝短期成功的部分响应。 所有内容都从同一种子以相同的字节方式重播。 Dusty 是一个惰性依赖项，此目标不是默认测试步骤的一部分。

zig build validate-dusty

这是 std.Io.net 边界的外部式功能演示，而不是第三方 SUT 发现。 0.6 分片链已完成：池化保活重用和大字节精确传输与池和传输场景一起落地，还发现了两个已确认的灰尘错误（请参阅 FOUND_BUGS.md），并且选择加入任务启动抖动让种子扫描探索启动顺序，例如监听前连接竞赛。

队列客户端验证

可选的 validate-beanstalkz 目标针对线束拥有的内存中 beanstalkd 运行固定的、未修改的 g41797/beanstalkz beanstalkd 工作队列客户端，该 beanstalkd 通过模拟的 std.Io.net 流使用文本协议。 它涵盖了带有埋入/踢出状态转换的生产/消费往返行程、顺序连接搅动（新连接、放置、退出、关闭（.both）、按 FIFO 顺序耗尽的关闭周期）、在五秒虚拟发布延迟中停放的超时阻塞保留，以及停放保留下的服务器进程崩溃：幸存的客户端通过重置唤醒，该重置表现为库的 CommunicationFailure 合约，然后注册的进程重新启动以新的形式恢复。 所有内容都从同一种子以相同的字节方式重播。 beanstalkz 是一个惰性依赖项，此目标不是默认测试步骤的一部分。

zig build validate-beanstalkz

register.write.start version=1 value=41 retry_limit=8
register.message kind=propose to=0 version=1 value=41
replica.accept replica=0 version=1 value=41 accepted=true
register.message kind=propose to=1 version=1 value=41
replica.accept replica=1 version=1 value=41 accepted=true
register.write.quorum version=1 value=41 acks=2

地位

木偶还早呢 这是 0.x 版本：1.0 之前没有 API 稳定性保证。 今天预期稳定的表面是 World、Env、Control、SimCase、runSimCase / ExpectSim*、Disk、SimDisk、RealDisk、Production 和 Recorder。 公共端点（消息）消息建模表面仍然是实验性的，同时其所有权和传输契约根据真实的 SUT 进行验证。

该模拟器当前对时钟、确定性随机性、磁盘、目录感知 std.Io.File/Dir 子集、实验类型消息建模、窄调度程序支持的 std.Io.net 流子集（具有接受/读取暂停以及延迟和发送时间损失）、交付时间分区、确定性修复和纯文本主机查找（未修改的 std.http.Client 在模拟服务器上运行；真正的 DNS 不受支持）以及协作 std.Io 任务、组和futex 等待互斥体/条件代码，针对固定的 g41797/mailbox 和 g41797/beanstalkz 目标以及内部有界队列功能演示以及固定的 Ochi 存储目标进行验证。 它不模拟任意操作系统线程调度或内存级并发；依赖于那些需要单独测试的代码。 模拟器还通过 Env.allocator() 和协作取消对确定性分配错误进行建模：Future.cancel 和 Group.cancel 传递错误。遵循 std.Io 的一次性协议，在 futex、睡眠和网络挂起点取消。 一次性 sim.transitionToLiveness(core) 会结束故障状态，因此有界运行可以证明一旦故障停止，核心就会取得进展。 网络有两个兄弟测试高度。 节点范围的 std.Io.net 是编解码器、帧、部分 I/O 和流生命周期的规范文字相同代码路径。 实验端点（消息）探索网络之上的协议/状态机行为；生产使用应用程序拥有的传输接缝，Marionette 并不声称真正的传输通过端点模型运行。 以前 Marionette 拥有的生产适配器在 0.6 中被删除。 计划中的队列暂停和更广泛的调度程序奇偶校验。

支持调度程序的光纤在 Linux 和 macOS 上进行了测试。 x86_64 Windows 光纤路径被故意禁用，直到其 Win64 条目 ABI 具有执行覆盖率。 RealDisk.syncDir 返回 error.DirectorySyncUnsupported，因为 Zig 0.16 不公开可移植的目录同步操作；它从不报告其未执行的耐久性。

如果您正在构建确定性很重要的东西并且您想尝试一下，那么示例/目录是最好的起点。 欢迎开放问题和 PR。
